transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
Following today's resignation of NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang,
following reports of extramarital affairs,
including one with a suspected Chinese spy,
the chip-making company Key to Artificial Intelligence
is looking for a way forward.
NPR's John Ruitz says Huang's resignation is raising a lot of questions.
>> There's a lot we don't know about the spy allegations,
which NPR has not independently confirmed and which China denies.
We don't know if any NVIDIA information might have been compromised
or national security for that matter.
The U.S. bans the export of NVIDIA's best chips to China,
so that's why allegations that Huang was involved with someone
who might have been a spy for China are so alarming.
Second, the company faces uncertainty.
Jensen Huang was, by all accounts, a micromanager.
He had his hand in loads of decisions at the company, big and small.
Dozens of senior employees looked to him for direct guidance,
and Jensen Huang had no apparent succession plan.
>> New York Senator Chuck Schumer has an opponent
for Senate Majority Leader when the new Congress meets in January.
Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen announced his intention
to challenge Schumer in a social media post.
After a close election, Democrats will hold on to the governor's office in Kansas.
State Senator Cindy Holscher's win extends Democratic victories
following last week's midterm elections from Kansas Public Radio's Zach Boblett reports.
>> Despite Kansas having 400,000 more registered Republicans than Democrats,
voters decided to keep a Democrat in the governor's office.
Holscher will replace fellow Democrat Laura Kelly,
who leaves office in January after two terms.
Holscher ran a populist campaign focused on funding special education,
property tax relief, and a data center moratorium.
She beat a Republican backed early by President Trump.
The Kansas legislature is controlled by Republicans,
but they lost seats in the midterms,
which will make it easier for Holscher to veto bills.
For NPR News, I'm Zach Boblett in Topeka.
>> White House on-boys Steve Whitkoff and Jared Kushner
are on their way to meet with Ukraine's president tonight
after Russia's Vladimir Putin hosted them at the Kremlin.
Here's NPR's Charles Maines reporting.
Whitkoff and Kushner arrived in Moscow to personally brief Putin
on two days of U.S.-led peace talks
between Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi.
Those discussions focused heavily on European security issues.
A topic Kushner suggested could unlock a wider peace
if Russia would drop objections to European representatives joining.
A request Whitkoff later said Putin endorsed.
Yet Putin accused Europe of prolonging the conflict
through its military support to Kiev
and signaled Russia's ambitions
to seize more Ukrainian territory remained unchanged.
It's a message Whitkoff and Kushner will deliver to Ukrainian president
Vladimir Zelensky and European officials when they gather in Ireland.
Charles Maines, NPR News, Moscow.
>> And you're listening to NPR News.
The cause of Wednesday's collapse
of a three-story apartment building in New York City remains unclear.
The investigation is ongoing.
The building fell without warning.
Officials say eight people were killed,
including two children and two construction workers
who were part of a crew working in a neighboring lot.
Officials say the search for victims came to an end today.
SpaceX is preparing another test launch of its massive Starship rocket.
NPR's Jeff Brumfield reports that some worry
it may be leaving behind a key partner.
>> Starship is the largest rocket ever built.
It's super powerful.
>> Three, two, one.
>> But it can't carry humans into orbit.
That job falls to a much smaller rocket called Falcon 9,
which SpaceX now plans to retire.
Falcon 9 has been a workhorse for NASA,
which uses it to reach the International Space Station,
but Tim Ferrar with TMF Associates says SpaceX isn't earning enough
from launching astronauts.
>> It's not making a lot of money out of NASA,
although it seems likely that the individual missions are profitable.
They're small potatoes.
>> Ferrar says NASA contracts saved SpaceX from bankruptcy
over a decade ago, but to date,
the company sees more profit from satellite Internet
and eventually data centers in space.
Jeff Brumfield, NPR News.
>> Turning to global markets following a week
capped by the resignation of NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang,
stocks in Asia are a mix following modest losses on Wall Street.
All three major indices fell four-tenths of a percent.
I'm Giles Snyder. This is NPR News.

topics.text: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid reports of extramarital affairs, including one with suspected Chinese spy
Kansas Democrat Cindy Holscher wins governor's race, defeating Republican backed by Trump
Witkoff and Kushner brief Putin in Moscow after Abu Dhabi Ukraine peace talks
Investigation continues into Wednesday collapse of three-story New York City apartment building that killed eight
SpaceX plans to retire Falcon 9 rocket, raising concerns about losing NASA launch partner
Asian stocks mixed after modest losses on Wall Street, with major indices down four-tenths of a percent
